sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:65

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:65:1
items.html:
The more the Partzufim proceed and descend from their level, the more their separation is revealed — the aspect of MA from the aspect of BON: And this depends on the measure of the flaw that is in BON. And it has already been brought above that there are three aspects in this (page 624, the passage beginning “And with this you will understand”, see there): for what came out in Nekudim in the aspect of Katnut, from the substance of their own emanation, is the first aspect, the choicest in BON, and Atik took it. And what came out there in the aspect of addition, by the coupling of AB and SAG, which illuminated through the Tabur to the GAR of Nekudim, lowered the bottom Hey from the Einayim of the Keter to the Peh of Nekudim, and restored the GAR to the upper AVI, is the second aspect of BON, inferior to the first aspect, because the matter of the nullification occurred in it, since it came out in the aspect of addition; and AA and the upper AVI took it. And what came out there by the MAN of the Vav and the point, which illuminated through the Yesod of AK — namely, from the aspect of the coupling of the look of the eyes of the upper AVI, one into the other, and onward — is the third aspect of BON, the worst of all, from which the GAR of Atzilut, which are Atik, AA and the upper AVI, took nothing for the correction of the substance of their Partzufim; but ZON, of necessity, took from it, for this Vav and point of the Yesod of AK, which became MAN in the AVI of Nekudim, are the entire substance of ZA, being the aspect of the seminal root drop of ZA, as written in Part 7, study it there well.
And therefore, the MA and BON of Atik are attached to one another with a most wondrous attachment, because in the BON that Atik took there is no flaw whatsoever, for no nullification whatsoever occurred in it at the time of the breaking of the vessels. And the MA and BON of AA are inferior to the MA and BON of Atik, for in his BON a nullification already occurred, and therefore the difference between his MA and his BON is discernible, in the aspect of right and left; unlike Atik, which is entirely right. And in the MA and BON of the upper AVI there is a greater difference, for they became two bodies, except that they are attached to one another in one wall, face to face, as above. However, in each of them there is MA and BON in a complete attachment, face to face, for in Aba there is MA and BON, and in Ima there is MA and BON, as above in the adjacent item, see there. But in ZA there is a great difference and separation between his MA and his BON, since he is of the third aspect, the worst of all; and therefore the MA and BON in him stand back to back.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:65:2
items.html:
The ZA is entirely the aspect of MA, and the Nukva is entirely the aspect of BON, and they are separated, at times back to back and at times face to face: This does not contradict what the ARI wrote in Etz Chaim, Gate 20, Chapter 10, that ZA took the VAK of BON and the VAK of MA, and the Nukva took the Malchut of MA and the Malchut of BON, see there. There is thus MA and BON in ZA, and MA and BON in the Nukva; and how does he say here that ZA is entirely MA and the Nukva is entirely BON? And the matter is that ZON too were divided into two Partzufim at the Chazeh within them, like the upper AVI, called the great ZON and the small ZON, as the ARI wrote in the adjacent item; in such a manner that the VAK of MA and the VAK of BON are called the great ZON — that is, ZA and Rachel, who are equal in their stature — and the Malchut of MA and the Malchut of BON are called the small ZON — that is, Jacob and Rachel the small, or the Nukva of ZA. And it was explained above, in the adjacent item concerning the upper AVI, that the ARI speaks here of the time when the upper AVI and YESHSUT are included in a single Partzuf, see there. And likewise here, concerning ZON, he speaks of the time when the great ZON and the small ZON are included in a single Partzuf; at which time all the seven lower ones of MA are regarded as ZA, and all the seven lower ones of BON as the Nukva. For in the VAK of MA, called the great ZA, Jacob, who is the Malchut of MA, is included; and in the VAK of BON, called the great Rachel, the small Rachel is included. And in this state, ZA with Jacob is found to be entirely MA, and the great Nukva with the small Rachel is entirely BON. And what the above-mentioned Etz Chaim says, that ZA took the VAK of MA and the VAK of BON, refers to the great ZON together, both of whom are sometimes called by the name of ZA alone, and the VAK of BON is regarded as the Nukva within his body. And likewise, what he says, that the Nukva of ZA took the Malchut of MA and the Malchut of BON, refers to the small ZON, both of whom are sometimes called by the name of the Nukva of ZA.
And this is what he said, “The ZA is entirely the aspect of MA, and the Nukva is entirely the aspect of BON, and they are separated, at times back to back and at times face to face,” namely, as above: that ZA includes with him also the small Jacob, and there are now in them the seven lower ones of MA; and the great Nukva includes also the small Rachel, and there are now in them the seven lower ones of BON. And they are regarded as separated from one another, for even when they are attached to one another, they are then in the aspect of back to back, which is regarded as separation. And when they are face to face, they are indeed separated from one another completely. And this is what he said: at times back to back, which is regarded like separation, and at times face to face, in which case they are literally separated.
